title: Inhibition That Moves Nothing at Rest

scenes.tts: Can an input stop a spike without moving a resting cell's voltage at all?
scenes.visual: A flat resting trace and, beside it, a dashed threshold line. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Can an input stop a spike without moving a resting cell's voltage at all?

scenes.tts: Our cell starts at rest. Alone, the five nanosiemens excitatory input would carry it toward minus 43, past threshold. It would fire on the way.
scenes.caption: Our cell starts at rest. Alone, the 5 nS excitatory input would carry it toward −43 mV, past threshold. It would fire on the way.
scenes.visual: The voltage scale: grey leak rope at −65 mV, red AMPA rope at 0 mV. A dashed ghost marker labelled 'excitation alone, passive prediction −43.3 mV' rises from −65 mV and crosses the dashed threshold at −50 mV; a spark marks the spike.
scenes.narration: Our cell starts at rest. Alone, the 5 nS excitatory input would carry it toward −43 mV, past threshold. It would fire on the way.

scenes.tts: Now meet an inhibitory rope of ten nanosiemens. It is tied exactly at rest, minus 65 millivolts.
scenes.caption: Now meet an inhibitory rope of 10 nS. It is tied exactly at rest, −65 mV.
scenes.visual: A blue rope labelled shunt, 10 nS, is drawn with its peg at −65 mV, right beside the leak's peg.
scenes.narration: Now meet an inhibitory rope of 10 nS. It is tied exactly at rest, −65 mV.

scenes.tts: First, what does this rope do to a resting cell?
scenes.visual: The red rope is off; the marker sits at −65 mV. On screen: Pause. What does the shunt do at rest?
scenes.narration: First, what does this rope do to a resting cell?

scenes.tts: Nothing. Its rope is tied exactly where the marker sits, so it pulls on nothing. The trace stays at minus 65.
scenes.caption: Nothing. Its rope is tied exactly where the marker sits, so it pulls on nothing. The trace stays at −65 mV.
scenes.visual: The blue rope hangs slack. The Vm trace below stays flat at −65 mV. On screen only: (−650 − 650)/20 = −65 mV.
scenes.narration: Nothing. Its rope is tied exactly where the marker sits, so it pulls on nothing. The trace stays at −65 mV.

scenes.tts: Now start again from rest, and switch on the excitation and the shunt together. Where does the marker head?
scenes.visual: The red rope returns together with the blue rope; the marker sits at −65 mV. On screen: Pause. Excitation plus shunt from rest: where does the marker settle?
scenes.narration: Now start again from rest, and switch on the excitation and the shunt together. Where does the marker head?

scenes.tts: Toward minus 52 millivolts. That is below threshold, so the cell never fires.
scenes.caption: Toward −52 mV. That is below threshold, so the cell never fires.
scenes.visual: The marker rises from −65 mV and settles at −52.0 mV, never crossing the dashed threshold line. On screen only: −1300/25 = −52.0 mV. Label: no spike.
scenes.narration: Toward −52 mV. That is below threshold, so the cell never fires.

scenes.tts: The shunt's top-line term is zero, so it adds nothing to the top. It acts through the bottom line, the total conductance.
scenes.visual: The from-rest formula: the shunt's top-line term reads 10 × 0 = 0; the bottom line grows from 15 to 25.
scenes.narration: The shunt's top-line term is zero, so it adds nothing to the top. It acts through the bottom line, the total conductance.

scenes.tts: The depolarization falls from about 22 millivolts to 13.
scenes.caption: The depolarization falls from about 22 mV to 13 mV.
scenes.visual: A bar pair: 21.7 mV without the shunt, 13.0 mV with it. On screen only: × 15/25 = 0.60.
scenes.narration: The depolarization falls from about 22 mV to 13 mV.

scenes.tts: This is shunting inhibition. It moves nothing at rest.
scenes.visual: Label: shunting inhibition. A flat resting trace with the note 'invisible at rest'.
scenes.narration: This is shunting inhibition. It moves nothing at rest.

scenes.tts: It shows itself when something else tries to move the voltage. Then it cuts that movement.
scenes.visual: Excitation arrives; with the shunt, the trace rises less than a ghost trace without it.
scenes.narration: It shows itself when something else tries to move the voltage. Then it cuts that movement.

scenes.tts: The shunt is a rope tied where the marker already sits. It holds the marker back whenever another rope drags it away.
scenes.visual: The marker is dragged right by the red rope; the blue rope tightens and pulls it back toward −65 mV. On screen only: at −52 mV, 10 nS × 13 mV = 130 pA back toward rest.
scenes.narration: The shunt is a rope tied where the marker already sits. It holds the marker back whenever another rope drags it away.

scenes.tts: Electrically, the shunt lowers input resistance. Excitation moves the voltage less, whether it is a synaptic conductance or injected current.
scenes.visual: Two small icons: a synapse and an electrode. Both produce smaller voltage changes with the shunt on.
scenes.narration: Electrically, the shunt lowers input resistance. Excitation moves the voltage less, whether it is a synaptic conductance or injected current.

scenes.tts: It changed only the bottom line.
scenes.visual: Banner: the shunt changed only the bottom line.
scenes.narration: It changed only the bottom line.

scenes.tts: The shunt does a second thing. It shortens the time constant.
scenes.visual: On screen: τ_eff = C / total g. The bottom line grows; τ shrinks.
scenes.narration: The shunt does a second thing. It shortens the time constant.

scenes.tts: Now switch off the excitation, and let the cell return to rest. With the leak and the shunt open, tau is 10 milliseconds. That is half the leak's 20.
scenes.caption: Now switch off the excitation, and let the cell return to rest. With the leak and the shunt open, τ is 10 ms. That is half the leak's 20 ms.
scenes.visual: The red rope disappears and the marker returns to −65 mV. On screen only: τ = 200 pF / 20 nS = 10 ms (all three open: 200/25 = 8 ms; leak alone: 20 ms).
scenes.narration: Now switch off the excitation, and let the cell return to rest. With the leak and the shunt open, τ is 10 ms. That is half the leak's 20 ms.

scenes.tts: That is cell B from the summation chapter.
scenes.visual: Cell B's bookmarked panel from chapter 2 slides in beside the scale.
scenes.narration: That is cell B from the summation chapter.

scenes.tts: Give it two brief pulses again, ten milliseconds apart. Less of the first is left for the second to ride on.
scenes.caption: Give it two brief pulses again, 10 ms apart. Less of the first is left for the second to ride on.
scenes.visual: Two EPSP traces overlaid: without the shunt (τ = 20 ms) and with it (τ = 10 ms). On screen only: 3.21 mV vs 2.74 mV.
scenes.narration: Give it two brief pulses again, 10 ms apart. Less of the first is left for the second to ride on.

scenes.tts: In this idealized case, each jump stays the same size. Only the tail is shorter.
scenes.visual: The two initial jumps are marked equal (2 mV each); the shunted tail is highlighted as shorter.
scenes.narration: In this idealized case, each jump stays the same size. Only the tail is shorter.

scenes.tts: A real synaptic current flows for a millisecond or more. While it flows, the shunt drains charge, so the peak is smaller too.
scenes.visual: Above, a synaptic current pulse lasting a few ms, labelled synaptic current. Below, an EPSP with a much longer membrane decay: with the shunt, its peak is lower and its tail shorter than without.
scenes.narration: A real synaptic current flows for a millisecond or more. While it flows, the shunt drains charge, so the peak is smaller too.

scenes.tts: A shunt tied at rest moves nothing at rest. It shows itself as smaller EPSPs and less summation.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: tied at rest, it moves nothing at rest; it shows as smaller EPSPs and less summation.
scenes.narration: A shunt tied at rest moves nothing at rest. It shows itself as smaller EPSPs and less summation.
